courses.title: Passive Assist Technology
moduleTitles: Blind Spot and Cross Traffic Alerts

questions.prompt: What does a forward-facing collision avoidance camera primarily detect ahead of the vehicle?
questions.explanation: The forward camera detects vehicles, pedestrians, and lane markings ahead.

questions.prompt: In a camera-type collision avoidance system, what usually happens first as a collision risk rises?
questions.explanation: Warning comes first; braking support follows if the driver does not respond.

options.label: C
options.body: A visual/audible warning is given, then braking support if needed

questions.prompt: Which condition most reduces forward camera collision detection accuracy?
questions.explanation: Dirt, fog, and heavy rain obscure the camera and reduce detection.

options.label: B
options.body: Dirt, fog, or heavy rain obscuring the camera view

questions.prompt: A passive lane departure system differs from an active system because it:
questions.explanation: Passive means warn only; active systems add steering correction.

options.label: A
options.body: Steers the vehicle back into the lane automatically

options.label: B
options.body: Only warns the driver and does not apply steering correction

options.label: C
options.body: Brakes the vehicle to a stop

questions.prompt: How does a passive lane departure system typically alert the driver?
questions.explanation: Lamp/chime plus wheel or seat vibration is the typical passive alert.

options.label: A
options.body: Horn, high beams, and hazard lights

options.label: B
options.body: Warning lamp/chime and often steering wheel or seat vibration

questions.prompt: A passive lane departure system will normally NOT warn when:
questions.explanation: Signalling suppresses the warning for an intended lane change.

options.label: A
options.body: The turn signal is on for an intended lane change

options.label: B
options.body: The vehicle is travelling in a straight line

questions.prompt: Blind spot monitoring sensors are most commonly located:
questions.moduleTitle: Blind Spot and Cross Traffic Alerts
questions.explanation: Blind spot radar sensors sit at the rear bumper corners.

questions.prompt: When a vehicle is detected in the blind spot, the driver is usually warned by:
questions.moduleTitle: Blind Spot and Cross Traffic Alerts
questions.explanation: A mirror indicator warns, often with a chime if you signal toward the vehicle.

options.label: A
options.body: An indicator in or near the side mirror, often with a chime if signalling

questions.prompt: Rear cross traffic alert is most useful when:
questions.moduleTitle: Blind Spot and Cross Traffic Alerts
questions.explanation: Cross traffic alert is designed for reversing out with limited side visibility.

options.label: B
options.body: Reversing out of a parking space with limited side visibility

questions.prompt: Rear cross traffic alert warns about:
questions.moduleTitle: Blind Spot and Cross Traffic Alerts
questions.explanation: It warns of vehicles approaching from either side behind you.

options.label: B
options.body: Vehicles approaching from the left or right behind the vehicle

options.label: D
options.body: Pedestrians directly in front of the grille

courses.title: Advanced Driver Assist System
moduleTitles: Understanding the Operation Principles of ADAS
The Autonomous Vehicle Brain ADAS and Artificial Intelligence

questions.prompt: ADAS features are best described as systems that:
questions.explanation: ADAS assists the driver; it does not remove the need for attention.

options.label: A
options.body: Replace the driver completely on all roads

options.label: B
options.body: Assist the driver with sensing, warnings, and partial control tasks

options.label: D
options.body: Remove the need for driver attention

questions.prompt: The basic ADAS operating cycle is:
questions.moduleTitle: Understanding the Operation Principles of ADAS
questions.explanation: Sense, process/decide, then warn or act is the core ADAS cycle.

options.label: B
options.body: Sense, process/decide, then warn or act

questions.prompt: Ultrasonic sensors are best suited to:
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic range is short, ideal for parking and low speeds.

options.label: B
options.body: Short-range, low-speed detection such as parking

questions.prompt: Automotive radar determines a target's speed mainly by using:
questions.explanation: Radar uses the Doppler shift of reflected radio waves for target speed.

options.label: A
options.body: The Doppler effect on reflected radio waves

options.label: B
options.body: The colour of the target vehicle

questions.prompt: A key strength of ADAS cameras compared with radar is:
questions.explanation: Cameras classify objects — signs, pedestrians, lane lines — radar cannot.

options.label: B
options.body: Classifying what an object is, such as a sign, pedestrian, or lane line

options.label: C
options.body: Measuring distance most accurately at long range

options.label: D
options.body: Working with the lens fully blocked

questions.prompt: LIDAR builds a 3D view of surroundings by:
questions.explanation: LIDAR times laser pulse reflections (time of flight) to build a 3D map.

options.label: A
options.body: Timing reflected laser pulses (time of flight)

questions.prompt: Vehicle localization means determining:
questions.explanation: Localization is the vehicle's precise position in its environment/map.

options.label: B
options.body: The vehicle's precise position within its environment/map

questions.prompt: V2X communication allows a vehicle to exchange information with:
questions.explanation: V2X means vehicle-to-everything: vehicles, infrastructure, and networks.

questions.prompt: In an autonomous/ADAS control unit, artificial intelligence is mainly used to:
questions.moduleTitle: The Autonomous Vehicle Brain ADAS and Artificial Intelligence
questions.explanation: AI interprets sensor data, predicts behaviour, and supports decisions.

options.label: B
options.body: Interpret sensor data, predict behaviour, and support driving decisions

questions.prompt: Sensor fusion means:
questions.moduleTitle: The Autonomous Vehicle Brain ADAS and Artificial Intelligence
questions.explanation: Sensor fusion combines multiple sensors into one reliable picture.

options.label: B
options.body: Combining camera, radar, and other sensor inputs into one reliable picture

options.label: C
options.body: Using only one sensor for every task

options.label: D
options.body: Turning sensors off at highway speed

courses.title: ADAS Calibration Guide
moduleTitles: ADAS Rear Camera and All Round Vision Calibration

questions.prompt: Front camera calibration is typically required after:
questions.explanation: Windshield replacement or camera refit changes aim, so calibrate.

questions.prompt: Static camera calibration is performed:
questions.explanation: Static calibration is stationary with targets at specified positions.

options.label: B
options.body: Stationary, using targets placed at specified positions

questions.prompt: Before static calibration, the workshop area should be:
questions.explanation: A level floor, correct lighting, and target space are required.

options.label: B
options.body: Level, with correct lighting and space for targets

options.label: C
options.body: Dark with the vehicle on a lift at full height

questions.prompt: Dynamic camera calibration differs because it is completed:
questions.explanation: Dynamic calibration completes during a specified road drive.

options.label: B
options.body: During a specified road drive while the system learns lane markings

questions.prompt: All-round (360-degree) vision systems create a bird's-eye view by:
questions.moduleTitle: ADAS Rear Camera and All Round Vision Calibration
questions.explanation: All-round vision stitches multiple camera images into a bird's-eye view.

options.label: B
options.body: Stitching together images from multiple cameras

options.label: C
options.body: Using only the rear camera zoomed out

questions.prompt: If rear camera calibration is incorrect, the most likely symptom is:
questions.moduleTitle: ADAS Rear Camera and All Round Vision Calibration
questions.explanation: Wrong rear calibration distorts the image and misplaces guide lines.

options.label: A
options.body: Distorted image or parking guide lines that do not match vehicle path

questions.prompt: Front radar calibration mainly ensures:
questions.explanation: Radar calibration aligns aim to the vehicle's thrust line.

options.label: A
options.body: The radar aims correctly relative to the vehicle's thrust line

questions.prompt: Front radar calibration should be checked after:
questions.explanation: Bumper, bracket, or collision work can move the radar — check calibration.

options.label: A
options.body: Front bumper / radar bracket repair or collision work

questions.prompt: A scan tool is used during radar calibration to:
questions.explanation: The scan tool starts the routine and reads values and fault codes.

options.label: A
options.body: Start the calibration routine and read alignment values / fault codes

questions.prompt: If calibration is skipped after windshield replacement, the lane/forward systems may:
questions.explanation: Skipped calibration can offset detection or set fault codes.

options.label: B
options.body: Detect objects offset from their true position or set fault codes

questions.prompt: Traction control primarily prevents:
questions.explanation: Traction control limits driven wheel spin during acceleration.

questions.prompt: Traction control can reduce wheel spin by:
questions.explanation: It brakes the spinning wheel and/or reduces engine torque.

options.label: B
options.body: Braking the spinning wheel and/or reducing engine torque

questions.prompt: Traction control detects wheel spin mainly by comparing:
questions.explanation: Differing wheel speeds reveal a spinning wheel.

questions.prompt: Stability control (ESC) helps the driver by:
questions.explanation: ESC keeps the vehicle heading where the driver steers in a skid.

options.label: A
options.body: Keeping the vehicle heading where the driver steers during a skid

questions.prompt: Which sensor is essential for ESC to detect a skid / unwanted rotation?
questions.explanation: The yaw rate sensor detects unwanted rotation about the vertical axis.

questions.prompt: To correct oversteer, ESC will typically:
questions.explanation: Braking an individual wheel creates a correcting yaw moment.

options.label: A
options.body: Brake an individual wheel (often the outer front) to create a correcting yaw moment

options.label: C
options.body: Turn the steering for the driver fully

questions.prompt: Launch control is designed to provide:
questions.explanation: Launch control gives fast, repeatable starts with controlled RPM/spin.

options.label: A
options.body: The slowest possible start to save fuel

options.label: B
options.body: Fast, repeatable standing starts with controlled RPM and wheel spin

questions.prompt: During launch control activation, the system typically holds:
questions.explanation: It holds a preset launch RPM until release.

options.label: A
options.body: Engine RPM at a preset launch limit until the clutch/brake is released

questions.prompt: Hill descent control helps on steep downhill grades by:
questions.explanation: Hill descent brakes individual wheels to hold a low set speed downhill.

options.label: A
options.body: Automatically braking individual wheels to hold a low set speed

questions.prompt: While hill descent is active, the driver can usually adjust target speed with:
questions.explanation: Cruise switches adjust target speed; pedals override the system.

options.label: B
options.body: Cruise control speed switches, and override with brake/accelerator

questions.prompt: The wiper park position is controlled so that blades:
questions.explanation: Park control returns blades to the base of the windshield at switch-off.

options.label: A
options.body: Stop in the middle of the windshield

options.label: B
options.body: Return to and stop at the base of the windshield when switched off

options.label: D
options.body: Lift off the glass at speed

questions.prompt: A rain sensor detects rain on the windshield mainly by:
questions.explanation: Rain sensors use changes in infrared reflection inside the glass.

options.label: B
options.body: Changes in infrared light reflected within the glass

questions.prompt: A head-up display (HUD) helps the driver by:
questions.explanation: HUD projects key information in the forward line of sight.

options.label: A
options.body: Projecting key information in the driver's forward line of sight

questions.prompt: A direct TPMS system measures tire pressure using:
questions.explanation: Direct TPMS uses a pressure sensor in each wheel.

options.label: B
options.body: A pressure sensor in each wheel/valve

questions.prompt: Wireless phone charging in a vehicle works by:
questions.explanation: Wireless charging transfers power inductively from pad to phone.

options.label: B
options.body: Inductive power transfer from a charging pad to the phone

questions.prompt: An immobilizer (mobilizer) system prevents starting unless:
questions.explanation: The immobilizer allows starting only with a recognised coded key.

options.label: B
options.body: A correctly coded key/transponder is recognised

options.label: C
options.body: The radio code is entered daily

questions.prompt: Keyless entry / passive entry allows locking and unlocking when:
questions.explanation: Passive entry works when the fob is near and the handle is touched/pulled.

options.label: A
options.body: The fob is nearby and a door handle sensor/switch is touched or pulled

options.label: B
options.body: The key is inserted in the ignition only

questions.prompt: A keyless entry system fails on one door only. The best first check is:
questions.explanation: One-door failure points to that handle, wiring, connector, and fault codes.

options.label: B
options.body: That door's handle sensor, wiring, and connector, plus fault codes

questions.prompt: Radar (adaptive) cruise control differs from conventional cruise control because it:
questions.explanation: Radar cruise keeps a set distance; conventional cruise holds speed only.

options.label: B
options.body: Automatically adjusts speed to keep a set distance from the vehicle ahead

questions.prompt: An autonomous / self-parking system typically uses ultrasonic sensors to:
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic sensors find/measure the space for assisted parking.

options.label: A
options.body: Find and measure a suitable parking space, then assist steering into it

questions.prompt: Before working on or near SRS components, you should:
questions.explanation: Disconnect the battery and wait the specified time before SRS work.

options.label: A
options.body: Disconnect the battery and wait the manufacturer-specified time

options.label: B
options.body: Probe airbag circuits with a test lamp

options.label: D
options.body: Short the airbag connector to ground

questions.prompt: Why must you never use an ohmmeter on a live airbag inflator circuit?
questions.explanation: Ohmmeter current can fire the inflator — never probe it that way.

options.label: A
options.body: It will flat the vehicle battery

options.label: B
options.body: Meter current could deploy the airbag

questions.prompt: An undeployed airbag module should be carried and stored:
questions.explanation: Carry/store undeployed modules cover facing away/up, clear and unstacked.

options.label: A
options.body: With the trim cover facing toward your body

options.label: B
options.body: With the trim cover facing away/up, on a clear bench, never stacked

options.label: C
options.body: In a hot oven to dry it

options.label: D
options.body: Loose in a toolbox with tools

questions.prompt: The SRS control unit decides to deploy by evaluating signals from:
questions.explanation: Crash/acceleration and safing sensor signals drive the deployment decision.

questions.prompt: The airbag inflates because the inflator:
questions.explanation: The inflator rapidly generates gas when ignited.

options.label: A
options.body: Uses compressed air from the tires

options.label: B
options.body: Rapidly generates gas when ignited by the deployment signal

options.label: C
options.body: Is pumped up by the driver

questions.prompt: After deployment begins, a frontal airbag inflates fully in approximately:
questions.explanation: Full inflation takes tens of milliseconds.

questions.prompt: The SRS warning lamp staying on after the bulb check indicates:
questions.explanation: A lamp staying on after bulb check means an SRS fault is stored.

options.label: B
options.body: A fault in the SRS system that needs diagnosis

questions.prompt: A seatbelt pre-tensioner works in a crash to:
questions.explanation: Pre-tensioners remove belt slack instantly in a crash.

options.label: B
options.body: Rapidly remove belt slack so the occupant is held firmly

questions.prompt: Most pre-tensioners are activated by:
questions.explanation: Most are pyrotechnic (some motor-driven), fired by the SRS unit.

options.label: B
options.body: A pyrotechnic charge (or motor) triggered by the SRS control unit

questions.prompt: After a crash in which a pre-tensioner fired, the correct action is to:
questions.explanation: A fired pre-tensioner is single-use — replace per manufacturer procedure.

options.label: A
options.body: Reuse it if the belt still clicks

options.label: B
options.body: Replace it as a single-use deployed component, following manufacturer procedure

options.label: C
options.body: Reset it with a hammer tap

options.label: D
options.body: Ignore it and clear codes only
